usual_baseline: Most core surgical trainees miss training standards. Nationally, 25.5% met the theatre standard and 5% met both standards [1547]. Only 25% of rotas met the standard, with a mean deficit of 18.5 sessions per 6 months [2125]. Regionally, 45% had consistent theatre access and 19% scheduled clinic time [2682].
fix_that_works: Presenting results to the trainee committee and trust leadership, with rota redesign, raised theatre access from 45% to 78% and clinic time from 19% to 50% [2682]. Rostering Advanced Clinical Practitioners onto trauma wards cut locum ward cover from 36.6% to 23.7% and saved £8,140 over three weeks [1229].
fix_that_fails: Over 75% of trainees still could not attend mandatory teaching after rota changes, and a later cycle fell back to 68% theatre and 39% clinic, with three trusts showing no progress [2682]. Protected theatre time stayed below 1 day/week despite ACP cover [1229].
consultant_advice: Surveys of trainee exposure are common and consistently show the same shortfall. The value lies in rota-level data that managers can act on, not questionnaires with low response rates. Measure protected theatre and clinic sessions actually worked, and teaching attendance, across repeated cycles.
